item.title: Early Retirement - Streetwise Hebrew Ep. 446
item.description: The word פרישה means retirement, and these days פרישה המוקדמת is on everyone's mind. Guy explains פרישה and other words from its root פרש.

item.title: The “‘We Did Nothing Special’: Remembering Uri Lupolianski” Edition - The Promised Podcast
item.description: Uri Lupolianski was the first ultra-Orthodox mayor of Jerusalem, and was convicted of corruption. A week after his death, Noah says that he was also a reflection of all of us, at our imperfect best.

item.title: When Everybody Is LGBT, Nobody Is - Tel Aviv Review
item.description: Amir Naaman and Dr Ran Heilbrunn discuss the next steps for queer theory after the impressive gains made by gay rights activism over the last few decades.

item.title: They're Exploiting the Situation - Streetwise Hebrew Ep. 447
item.description: The word נצלן is an exploiter - someone who’ll pump and dump you without giving it a second thought. This episode breaks down the word and its root נצל.

item.title: The “Ran’s Sheloshim” Edition - The Promised Podcast
item.description: Today marks the 30th day since we buried Ran Gvili, the last hostage to come home. Noah explores how wars end in Israel, and what the end of this war is like for all of us going through it.

item.title: Bubbe-Meises for the Masses: A Gendered Reading of the US Yiddish Press - Tel Aviv Review
item.description: At the turn of the 20th century, the Yiddish press in America didn’t just report the news; they offered advice, shaped politics, and helped newcomers navigate a bewildering new society.

item.title: The “Confounded, Unbounded & Undergrounded” Edition - The Promised Podcast
item.description: We discuss: 1) Whether we’re seeing a new, more Strangelovian PM Netanyahu 2) What life underground in the homefront tells us about Israeli society

item.title: Early Zionism's Arabists - Tel Aviv Review
item.description: A thought-provoking episode exploring how early Zionist thinkers engaged deeply with Arabic language and Islamic culture, challenging conventional views of identity and “Orientalism” in the Middle East.
